evidence.note: First run failed on torch.compile (missing C compiler) and 37.4M params too big for cap; diagnosed both, disabled compile, dropped tied lm_head, shrank to ~31M. Then OOM at batch 256 → reasoned single-lever reduction to 128. Targeted cause-based fixes, not random tweaks.

Fine-tune resume worsened val (2.776 vs 2.758); recognized it as a dead end, abandoned it, and reframed around the unused byte budget (28.6/32MB) to train a larger 60.8M int4 model — capacity-vs-size reasoning.

Key binding-constraint diagnosis: loaded int4 val (2.82) >> in-memory (2.667) identified quantization loss (not capacity/optimization) as the limiter; used 7.6MB headroom to move to mixed int8/int4 — trades quant scheme against accuracy within the cap (anchor-8).
Diagnosed per-row int4 scales as too coarse and switched to groupwise int4 (scales every 128), refining the quantization design against the byte budget.

Diagnosed that re-encoding an already-quantized static model can't recover accuracy; adapted to a fresh short fine-tune before group32 encoding — but these late experiments were partly redundant dead-ends pursued after weak evidence.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed the actual binding constraint from evidence — compile/size, OOM, capacity underuse, and most importantly the in-memory-vs-loaded quantization gap — and adapted the design accordingly, explicitly trading depth/width against the quantization scheme within the byte cap, which matches the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the decisive quant-loss diagnosis came only after a full 14k-iter run (sunk compute), it lost its earlier int8 checkpoint during a detour, and the closing group32/mixed re-encoding attempts were partly redundant dead-ends rather than early-abandoned, so corrections were compounding but not the clean frontier optimization of the top anchor.
